status: source review complete for packet source identities; applies to public/private fixed general specification; hidden runtime remains pending

rows.reason: DTO fields, public initializers and typed wireValue match the fixed API; only SwiftUI is imported and component is marked iOS 14. Runtime acquisition exists for this exact source hash, but no SDK was run in review.
Production @State holds nil selection, requested count and false flags. Reconciliation returns self for same snapshot and fully resets on changed request ID.
ForEach preserves model.options order. Selection resolves caller ID and availability, ignores same ID or sent state, clamps current count and clears acceptance.
Native minus/plus handlers pass -1/+1, disable outside inclusive selected limits or sent state, and update by one while clearing acceptance. Selection/revision clamp current count.

Int-cent multiplication/subtraction uses current option price/prepaid/credit. Formatter uses integer magnitude with literal ASCII dollar/point and two digits; negative, zero and positive copy/ink are distinct.

Credit starts false, its setter requires unsent positive credit and clears acceptance. New revision retains the choice only for positive credit; enabled expression uses zero because fixed API credit is nonnegative.
All meaningful edit paths clear acceptance; acceptance requires available current choice and unsent state. canSend requires choice, acceptance and unsent state.

View derives reconciled draft before drawing/actions and persists with onChange, using current model throughout; retains available ID with new bounds, otherwise clears only ID; clears acceptance/sent without keyed recreation.
Only submit invokes onSubmit after guards, constructing exact current typed values and then sent=true. All other handlers and reconciliation are callback silent; wire format is literal.

All eight base sizes use iOS 14 ScaledMetric, system fonts use declared regular/medium/semibold/bold roles; no scale cap or foreign font is present. This is source configuration, not computed font proof.

Production flow is non-scrolling leading VStacks with root16/section20, card12/radius16/border1, inside/option8, paragraph10, footer16 and rootRadius20. Text is vertical fixedSize without lineLimit or fixed height.
Actual Button labels define min64 choice, min44x44 quantity, and min52 send with 16 horizontal/14 vertical padding; text can grow vertically. Source dimensions do not establish physical hit areas.

Palette constants match, but initial Button labels use PlainButtonStyle plus disabled. Original current-source D0 PNGs show complete unavailable/sent choice labels and disabled send fill attenuated. Thus the independent no-whole-row-attenuation/source-style obligation fails; exact color is established only by native_pixels, not constants.

Leading alignment and caller arrays are preserved with no forced direction; native HStack holds quantity controls. Integer String interpolation and literal money formatter preserve the required ASCII format.

Production target IDs are unique per fixed unique option ID, current labels/selected traits are attached to Button/Toggle targets, and containers contain children. No duplicated UI or style readback is present. Actual OS behavior is a separate native obligation.
Fixed bridge decodes required fixture data into production DTO and forwards submission.wireValue without business derivation.
Fixed bridge directly calls imported production MenuChangeReviewPanel at one stable call site with no identity key, cloned view or outer product state.

Exact package, immutable data classes, composable API and typed wire format match fixed API; imports are existing Compose/Material3 only. Existing acquisition is hash-bound; no compilation was executed in review.
remember production draft starts with null choice/requested count/false flags, reconciles only on request or revision changes, and resets on new request ID.
Caller-order forEach resolves actual option IDs, excludes unavailable/sent choices, ignores same selection, clamps count and clears acceptance.
Native button handlers adjust by exactly one only inside inclusive bounds and while unsent. Disabled predicates, selection clamp and revised-bound clamp are explicit.

Int arithmetic derives signed balance from current price/prepaid/credit; integer-to-Long magnitude formatting yields ASCII dollar/point and two decimals without grouping. Null/zero/refund/payment render separately.
False initial credit is editable independently of selection while positive and unsent, edit clears acceptance, and reconciliation forces it false for zero credit.
Acceptance clears on selection/quantity/credit/revision edits; switch requires selected available option and unsent state, and canSend also requires accepted.

Current reconciled draft is derived/persisted before UI without keyed recreation. New fields are read directly from model; choice stays only if available and count clamps to current bounds; zero credit clears and acceptance/sent reset.
Only guarded send handler calls onSubmit with exact typed current values, then stores sent; all edit and caller-update paths are silent. Literal wireValue format matches API.
Native default system font uses approved 12/28/13/18/15/26/16/20 sp roles and weights, inheriting Compose font scale without caps. No computed text size is inferred.
Non-scrolling Columns/Rows use root16/section20, cards12/radius16/border1, inside/options8, notes10, footer16 and rootRadius20 dp. Text is unlimited and no fixed text height or ellipsis is set.
Actual Buttons have choice min64, quantity min44x44, send min52 and exact16/14 padding; heightIn/sizeIn preserve vertical growth. This establishes source dimensions only.

Every approved light/dark role is chosen explicitly. Option disabled content uses secondary ink with solid fill, not whole-row opacity; send enabled/disabled roles are explicit. MaterialTheme luminance selects caller theme.
Start alignment/TextAlign.Start and caller list order preserve native direction; no array reversal or forced text direction. Literal strings retain ASCII currency and counts.
